meta.title: Your server · Stored and exported data

cards.title: Settings and access: what the data means
items: Discord server ID and name, language, time zone, enabled features and custom emoji settings.
Discord roles allowed to use bot features and the channel selected for audit messages.
Stats settings: excluded voice channels, AFK channel, collection status and individual tracking preferences.
Installation dates, active/inactive server status and bot presence status. Old technical Stats observation timestamps are filtered in the export.

cards.title: Timers and war log: retained state and processing
items: Timer boards, associated channels and messages, settings, tracked assets, names, locations, owners and deadlines.
Alerts, acknowledgements, scheduled tasks, timer action history and synchronization status.
Server war-log subscriptions: faction, regions, destination channel, language, pause status and confirmed war.
Pending or delivered war-log notifications and board reset processing. Currently retained rows are copied into the file.

cards.title: Temporary voice: names only
items: PICKET stores template names, the destination Discord category, channel naming settings, capacity and idle timeout.
It also stores the deployment limit, private drafts, created channels, their occupants and verification/cleanup status.
The file contains only current template names. All options and operational data in this family are excluded.

cards.title: Stats: from observed members to their summaries
items: In the database: Discord IDs and names of observed members, plus IDs and names of observed voice channels.
Current presence, roles associated with voice periods, joins, moves, departures, presence periods and observation quality.
Private materialized summaries are also stored for service administration; they are excluded from the guild export.
In the file: Discord ID, name, accumulated voice time and last activity for each member represented in the last 60 days, plus a server summary.
Detailed events, individual periods, connected presence and the voice-channel list are not attached. Tracking settings and preferences belong to Settings and access.
The file also adds counts of events awaiting storage from the disk journal. This supplement is outside the database inventory shown here; its duration is not credited until processing.

cards.title: Logs and tracking: included records and one omission
items: Administration actions with their author and before/after values, server usage records and receipts preventing duplicate interaction processing.
Pending audit messages and their scheduling: these records are exported while retained.
Internal bot-departure request state is retained to execute or reconcile removal. It is excluded from the file; active/inactive status and audit records remain exported.

cards.title: Reading this comparison
items: The five families on the left form a functional inventory of server-scoped database records. Ordinary copies go straight to the file; only name selection and summary calculation need their own processing step.
The export is a snapshot of currently retained data, not a complete history or a backup that can restore everything.
The drawing follows the representation of database records. The supplement of pending voice-event counts is described in the Stats card.

An administrator requests the file under /picket settings → Data → Export. PICKET builds it in memory and sends it privately without retaining a copy. Exceeding the size limit produces no partial file.
